derivation.note: Mechanical field-name projection of the frozen blind-discovery.json for scripts/evaluate_blind_outputs.py. Generated post-reveal by script; no disposition, signal, or evidence content changed.

signals: Selecting 'Herbs' and then 'Vegetables' left all 6 cards visible (computed display 'block' on every non-matching card) — visible count never changed for any option.
The only observable effect was DOM reorder to strict alphabetical (Bee Balm…Lacinato Kale), identical for every category value — a sort, not a filter.
evidence: Operated: order_before [Genovese Basil, Lacinato Kale, Calendula, Cherry Radish, Common Chives, Bee Balm] -> order_after alphabetical; visible_after 6/6 for 'herb' and 'veg'.
evidence/WF-A-01.png; source: catfilter change handler sorts grid children by name (allowed-input source, lines ~81-88).
candidates.consequence: A shopper who selects 'Herbs' believes they are looking at only herbs; all categories remain on screen in a new order, so the catalogue cannot be narrowed and the control's label is false.
candidates.counterexample_tested: Considered that alphabetical sort might be the intended behavior with a mislabeled control; rejected — the label, the category option values, and the working search control beside it all establish a filtering idiom, and no sort affordance is announced.
candidates.title: 'Filter by category' sorts the catalogue alphabetically instead of filtering it

signals: URL is byte-identical before and after every view switch (no hash, query, or history entry), so no view can be bookmarked, deep-linked, or restored.

'Share this view' (clicked while Planting calendar was active) wrote the bare page URL to the clipboard — instrumented call recorded 'http://127.0.0.1:8907/checkout-flow.html' — then confirmed 'Copied'; a recipient lands on the default Catalogue, not the shared view.

Returning to Catalogue triggers a full location.reload(): the active search term 'kale' was erased (input empty after return) and the Planting view had already destroyed the grid node (grid count 0) rather than hiding it.
evidence: Operated URL/state/clipboard trace in probe results; evidence/WF-A-03.png, evidence/pageA-full.png.
candidates.consequence: The share affordance's promise is false and switching views silently discards the user's in-progress filtering; multi-state content cannot be linked, which also blocks the 'why would someone return' path.
candidates.counterexample_tested: Tab panels without URL state are a common SPA pattern and not inherently slop; rejected as innocent here because the page itself offers 'Share this view' (an explicit state-sharing promise it breaks) and uses a destructive reload instead of re-rendering.
candidates.title: View state has no address: share copies a stateless URL and returning to Catalogue destroys work in progress

signals: specificity — abstract filler dominates ('world's most advanced', 'cutting-edge technology', 'unparalleled results', 'unlock their full potential'): every sentence moves unchanged to any product in any industry; analyzer measured 2 abstract-filler matches against 1 concrete anchor in 31 words.
responsibility — the only number, 'Trusted by over 10,000 industry leaders', names no source, cohort, or date, and 'industry leaders' contradicts the page's stated audience of freelancers.
evidence: Quoted rendered text captured from the operated page; evidence/WF-B-01.png; analyzer receipt evidence/analyzer-WF-B-01.json (language en, sample 31 words / 3 sentences, adequacy insufficient for statistical cadence claims — none are made here).
Counter-surface: WF-B-02 on the same page states price, timeline, export format, reminder policy, and a working uptime link.
candidates.consequence: Users cannot tell what the product does or verify any claim; differentiation and trust both drop at the page's first proof moment.
candidates.title: Portable superlative claims with zero provenance replace the freelancer-specific reason the heading promises

signals: responsibility — rendered DOM shows four plain <span> badges with no link, title, citation, or source: '★★★★★ Rated 5/5 by users' (which users? how many? where?), '🏆 Best Invoicing Tool 2026' (awarded by whom?), '✔ Certified Excellence' (certified by whom, against what?).

specificity — 'Bank-grade security' and 'Certified Excellence' have no verifiable referent at all, and the unanimous 5/5 with no review count contrasts with the precise, sourced figures the same page proves it can publish (WF-B-02 uptime data).
evidence: Captured outerHTML of the badge row (no anchors, no attribution attributes); evidence/WF-B-03.png.
candidates.consequence: Unverifiable social proof at the decision point erodes trust in the whole page, including its true claims.
candidates.title: Self-awarded trust badges: no rater, no awarding body, no certifier, no linkable referent

signals: Keyboard/AT exclusion: the element is a SPAN with tabIndex -1, no role, and no accessible state; a full Tab traversal of the page reached 8 stops and never included it; even element.focus() fails to move focus to it.
Fake for pointer users too: clicking produced zero DOM change (page content byte-identical before and after) — the handler is empty, yet cursor:pointer and button styling invite the click.

Supporting failures in the same section: both inputs are placeholder-only (labels.length 0 — name disappears on entry), and the hint text measures 2.61:1 contrast at 13px (below the 4.5:1 minimum, WCAG 1.4.3).
evidence: Tab-sequence trace, focus probe, before/after DOM comparison, computed contrast; evidence/WF-C-01.png.
candidates.consequence: The section's only action is inoperable: keyboard and assistive-technology users cannot reach it, and mouse users who click it get silent nothing — defaults can never be applied, with no error, disabled state, or explanation.
candidates.counterexample_tested: Considered an intentionally disabled control awaiting input; rejected — there is no disabled attribute, styling, or explanatory state, and the cursor/styling actively affords clicking.
candidates.title: 'Apply defaults' is a fake control: a styled <span> that no one can reach by keyboard and that does nothing for anyone

signals: Fabricated precision: clicking Save at 22:05 displayed 'Saved at 09:30'; saving again displayed the identical '09:30' — the timestamp is hardcoded (source: new Date(2026,0,1,9,30)), so the specific-looking confirmation is false.
Broken persistence claim: after reload, both fields and the status were empty — the state the UI declared 'Saved' is gone on the very next page load.
evidence: Operated save/re-save/reload trace with real-clock comparison; evidence/WF-C-02.png.
candidates.consequence: A user cannot tell whether their latest save succeeded (every save reports the same moment), and data the UI confirmed as saved does not survive a refresh.
candidates.counterexample_tested: Tested the innocent readings: a deterministic demo timestamp and deliberately session-scoped persistence. Partially credited — hence moderate confidence and medium severity — but a reader-facing confirmation still asserts a specific wrong fact, and 'Saved' with no scope qualifier still overpromises. Genuine strengths retained in this sample: real <button>, visible focus style, and role='status' so the confirmation is announced.
candidates.title: Save confirmation asserts a fixed fabricated timestamp and a persistence it does not deliver

signals: Data loss: typed 'Please contact billing for records' into the close-account note, clicked 'Save changes', and the field was emptied — the value is discarded, not stored or redisplayed anywhere.

Zero feedback: no status text appeared (main text length delta 0), and the section contains no role=status or aria-live region — nothing confirms, denies, or explains; contrast with sibling WF-C-02 which at least confirms.
candidates.consequence: In the highest-stakes section of the page ('Danger zone', shown to clients at account closure), the user's writing vanishes on save with no confirmation, no error, and no recovery path — indistinguishable from success until it matters.
candidates.counterexample_tested: Considered an 'apply-and-clear' input idiom (like a chat box); rejected — a settings preference must redisplay its stored value, nothing anywhere shows the note was retained, and no confirmation exists to license the clearing.
candidates.title: 'Save changes' silently destroys the typed note and gives no feedback of any kind

cleared_suspicions.suspicion: Search might be cosmetic or mismatched with its promise, like the adjacent filter.
cleared_suspicions.why_cleared: The control does what it says, with feedback, keyboard access, and a working reset path.

cleared_suspicions.suspicion: Card-soup layout and small uppercase category text might fail hierarchy or contrast.
cleared_suspicions.why_cleared: Rendered evidence shows scannable hierarchy and passing contrast; no task friction observed in the grid itself (its filter failures belong to WF-A-01/WF-A-03).

cleared_suspicions.suspicion: Second claim block might be more of the same promotional filler; the '/uptime' link might be decorative.
cleared_suspicions.why_cleared: This is the counterexample that convicts WF-B-01: specific, attributable, actionable copy whose one link resolves to real data. Minor note (not a defect): link text '/uptime' resolves to an in-page section rather than a route.

cleared_suspicions.suspicion: Placeholder 'Invoice editor interface' frame might be synthetic proof — fake product imagery passed off as a real account.
cleared_suspicions.why_cleared: The synthetic-proof suspicion is disproven by honest disclosure: nothing is fabricated and the simulation is labeled. Replacing the placeholder with a real annotated screenshot is an enhancement opportunity, not a defect.

cleared_suspicions.suspicion: Toggle might be another fake or unannounced control; state text might be decorative.
cleared_suspicions.why_cleared: Control, state, feedback, and keyboard path all behave as promised. Minor note (not promoted): the #remindstate span carries no aria-live, but no functional announcement barrier was verified since aria-pressed on the focused button conveys the state.
